title: Adaptive Ingest Orchestrator for Console Event Streams
creator: Marco Rivera
description: We need a smarter, operationally resilient ingest layer for console metrics that adapts to workload patterns without losing fidelity for critical routes. The current monolithic Kafka consumer + enrichment fleet shows burst-driven latency spikes and expensive egress costs for high-cardinality routes. This ticket implements an Adaptive Ingest Orchestrator (AIO) that does three things: (1) route-aware pre-aggregation and sampling, (2) local deduplication and exactly-once-ish buffering using RocksDB state and idempotent output to Kafka topics, and (3) dynamic consumer shaping (switching from low-latency path to batched path based on SLO and queue depth). The orchestrator is implemented as a gRPC sidecar + controller service paired with stateful Flink processors for enrichment, with a lightweight fallback to a stateless fast-path transformer for latency-sensitive routes.
goals: Reduce 95th-percentile ingest latency from ~3.2s to <1.2s for low-cardinality routes
Decrease downstream tokenization/egress cost by 18% through adaptive pre-aggregation
Ensure no user-visible data loss for routes marked critical (preserve order and dedup by request_id)
Provide per-route backpressure signals surfaced to Console and SDKs
design_decisions: Use RocksDB-backed state in Flink jobs for local deduplication to avoid a separate global dedupe service
Implement adaptive sampling thresholds per-route stored in config service; default is lossless for routes tagged 'critical'
gRPC sidecar handles hot-shard routing and maintains short leases to distribute producer load evenly
Prefer Kafka as durable buffer (existing infra) and use a separate compacted topic for control signals
Trade-off: acceptance of eventual consistency for non-critical aggregated metrics in exchange for latency and cost improvements
implementation_notes: Sidecar exposes /health and /metrics; emits per-route queue depth and sample-rate metrics
Control plane stores per-route policies in config-service; updates are pushed via server-streaming gRPC to sidecars
Flink topology: ingestion -> enrich (stateful) -> route-splitter -> {fast-path|batch-path} -> kafka-out
Fast-path: stateless transform, gRPC sink to realtime aggregator; Batch-path: RocksDB state aggregation + windowed flush
Idempotency: use composite key (route + request_id) with TTL 24h for dedupe cache
Backpressure propagation: sidecar pauses upstream client connections when local buffer exceeds 75%
Telemetry: new high-cardinality histogram for per-route latency; integrate into console observability dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Canary at 5% traffic with feature flags and no production incidents for 72h
End-to-end freshness (producer->console dashboard) 95th < 5s for critical routes
Cost comparison report shows >=12% reduction in tokenization/egress cost for sampled cohort
Automated chaos tests (broker restart, partition rebalance) do not cause data loss for critical routes
testing_plan: Synthetic load: replay last 7 days' traffic scaled x10 to exercise hot routes
Game day: broker failover + network partition while canary running
Unit tests for dedupe TTL and RocksDB compaction behavior
Integration: validation harness against console dashboards to verify metric parity
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged canary: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over two weeks pending SLO metrics
Automated rollback if ingest lag 95th exceeds target or error rate > 0.5%
Post-rollout 14-day monitoring window with daily regression checks and cost review
